verdicts.reason:
I reproduced the core of this from the raw main transcript with my own script. The midpoint rule and the sentence composer were both changed after the output they affect had been produced and read.

**Midpoint rule.**
- Part A's readings finished at 17:07:39 EDT (21:07:39Z).
- At 21:08:57Z and 21:08:59Z the midpoint check became a requirement for READ. Before that edit, the builder docstring said the midpoint "is recorded and decides nothing".
- At 21:09:33Z the builder's own `text_checks` ran on `readings_run_A.json` and printed mid_ok False for A03, A04 and A09.
- At 21:09:59Z a character-versus-line comparison ran on the same returns. At 21:10:34Z the rule was rewritten to count by line. At 21:10:56Z all nine passed. Commit 450265ff followed at 21:11:15Z.
- Under the character rule those three sources are SKIMMED. So the switch moved the SURVEY's sworn counts `counts/read` (SURVEY line 45, now 30) and `counts/skimmed` (line 46, now 3), which would have been 27 and 6.
- The SURVEY's own bullet ("which failed three Part A readings") admits the failures were seen, which contradicts its lead sentence.

**Sentence composer.**
- The first build at 22:25:47Z printed "sentence: SURVIVES" and the doubled "without a floor, without a floor measured on the same weights".
- The edits followed at 22:27:01–22:27:19Z: the tie list, the phrase trimmer, and adding C5 to the `deleted` list.
- The rebuild at 22:27:59Z printed SURVIVES_WITHOUT_C5 and the repaired sentence. Commit a1886191 followed at 22:28:34Z.
- The result these repairs touched, the sentence and its status, was already known. The claim is false for this item under any reading of "result".

**Readings that might excuse it, and why they fail.**
- Reading "result" as clause statuses saves the midpoint item: Part B had not been listed at 21:10. It does not save the composer item.
- The repairs move toward the frozen rule rather than toward a preferred answer. That does not make the timing claim true.
- The midpoint proof is not in the frozen protocols; grep for midpoint or "middle third" finds nothing. So no clause status is wrong. But the SURVEY is a sworn document stating a false process claim, and it swears the counts that moved. The REPORT repeats the claim at lines 533–534. Under the lab's rubric (a sworn or public statement is false) this is a blocker.

**Where the finding overreaches.**
- CHANGELOG line 29 says "repaired before any result it touched was counted". That is defensible, since the repairs came before the record was built or committed.
- pr87_comment_pass4.md line ~52 says only "Each item is disclosed in the SURVEY and in the commits", which is true.
- The margins leg is weak. The margin prompt was necessarily written before its run. The margins builder was written at 22:27:42Z, 16 s before the last agent's transcript and the journal were last written (18:27:58 EDT). The margin check is not one of the disclosed items the sentence covers.
- The suggested repair's "all three are at distance 3 or 4" is wrong. A04 is at distance 2 in the record (A03 is 4, A09 is 3). The conclusion that no clause status could move still holds, because none is a candidate at distance 0.
- 450265ff's subject "committed before the builder runs on any return" is inaccurate, but the commit body discloses the character-first failure.

verdicts.reason:

It also matches the reason the lab gave for B04, another nature.com page: it opens with the site's browser-support notice and navigation and closes with a newsletter sign-up. Yet B12 is recorded as READ. The builder marks a source SKIMMED only when its ID is listed in the scope file, and the file lists only B04, B05 and B07.

B11 is a similar case the finding did not name: its own reader calls it "an alphaXiv landing page" that is "not the paper's full text", and it is also READ, though alphaXiv is not the publisher.

- The sworn numbers match the record as built.
- The SURVEY sentence says "Three located pages", so it is literally scoped to the located fetches, and B12 was a first-run fetch.
- The landing-page rule is in an input file, not in the frozen protocol text.

findings.title: Chauvin et al. described as grading the API comparison against an identical-weights null; that null grades the local TinyChange evaluation, while API endpoints are flagged by a 12-SD threshold
findings.claim: The SURVEY merges two setups into one sentence. The identical-weights null (1,000 original/original tests) scores the ROC AUC of local-model variants. Real API endpoints compared with their own earlier samples are flagged by a running 12-standard-deviation threshold with no stated level.
findings.evidence:
- texts\B22.txt line 318: 'We then perform 1,000 original/original hypothesis tests on each original model, to obtain the distribution of the statistic under the null hypothesis'.
- The first reader's reason (#/sources/B22/verdicts/C4a/reason): 'Real-world flags use a 12-standard-deviation threshold with no stated level'.
- margin-B22-1 object: 'graded in vitro by ROC AUC against 1,000 original/original tests, and applied to 189 real endpoints hourly with a running-variance threshold'.
- SURVEY lines 77-79: 'it compares an API endpoint's first-token log-probabilities with its own earlier samples, graded against a null from identical weights'.
findings.suggested_repair: Describe the two setups separately: an identical-weights null for the local variants, and a 12-SD running threshold for real API endpoints.

verdicts.reason:
I reproduced the conflation from the paper text and the record. The paper runs LT in two separate setups. (1) TinyChange, in vitro: local vLLM models are compared with their pruned, noised or fine-tuned variants, and detection is scored by ROC AUC against 1,000 original/original tests on identical weights. (2) 189 real endpoints: each endpoint is compared with itself over adjacent 24-sample windows, and a change is flagged by a running-mean + 12-SD threshold with a floor of 1.0. No identical-weights null is involved there. The SURVEY sentence joins the object of setup 2 ("an API endpoint's first-token log-probabilities with its own earlier samples") to the grading of setup 1 ("graded against a null from identical weights"). The paper never grades an endpoint-vs-earlier-self comparison that way. Two readers in the record describe the setups separately: the first reader's object field names both, and margin-B22-2 says "It is used in two setups". So the prose misdescribes what the record says.

I tried to refute it three ways, and none holds. First, the paper's generic framing ("a pair of LLM APIs (which can be the same API at different times)") does not rescue the sentence, because the original/original null only ever grades local models against their variants, never an endpoint against its own earlier samples. Second, the protocol's E3 does allow a floor "in the setup used for the comparison or for one of its sides", and the first reader coded the in-vitro object, so the record's E3=true, distance 1, missing E4 and the C4a status all stand. The defect is prose only. Third, "never sets a significance level" is accurate: alpha is symbolic and no p-values are reported.

Why minor and not blocker: the neighbour's identity, its distance, its missing element (E4) and every status are unchanged. The false part is a compressed sentence describing a neighbour's method, not a priced claim or a sworn span. The sworn spans at lines 76-79 cover only the distance numeral. It is still a factual misdescription inside a sworn document, so the repair has to go in a CORRECTION beside the SURVEY, not an edit. The same wording is not in the PR comment, the REPORT addendum or CHANGELOG (grep checked).

verdicts.reason:

The pass-4 protocol adds blind confirmers only for C4a. The builder demands two confirmers for C2 and C5 too, marks the source DISPUTED otherwise, makes the clause UNPRICED, and then deletes C5 while licensing the rest. Its own docstring states the inherited rule.

verdicts.reason:
I reproduced the mechanism. When a READ source gives C5 (or C2) a RETIRES with no confirmers, the builder marks it DISPUTED, sets the clause to UNPRICED and returns SURVIVES_WITHOUT_C5 (or SURVIVES_WITHOUT_C2). The docstring at build_sand_survey_pass4.py:29-30 says the opposite of what lines 201-213 do. That result is wrong under either reading of the frozen text:
- **Inherited rule only:** a READ RETIRES makes C5 RETIRED, and sentence rule 1 then retires the whole sentence.
- **Pass-4 amendments applied:** line 137 names the outcome of a disputed retirement, UNLICENSED. The protocol defines DISPUTED leading to UNPRICED and a deleted clause only for C4a (lines 63-64).

No frozen reading gives SURVIVES_WITHOUT_C5.

Two parts of the finding are overstated.
1. It says the protocol adds confirmers only for C4a. Line 135 of the pass-4 protocol also says "For every RETIRES: the two blind confirmations." So requiring confirmers for C2 and C5 has textual support. The lab also said so openly: builder commit 450265ff ("A RETIRES on C2 or C5 needs the same two confirmations"), sworn SURVEY line 16, REPORT line 503 and PR comment line 14 ("two blind confirmers for any retirement"). Demanding confirmers is therefore not itself a deviation. The defect is the outcome after a failed confirmation, plus the false docstring.
2. The severity is too high. The path never ran. No reading run has a C2 or C5 RETIRES, and no run has any confirmations. C5 is UNPRICED in the committed record only because B23 was UNFETCHABLE, which the inherited rule itself makes UNPRICED, and rule 2 deletes it. So SURVIVES_WITHOUT_C5 in the record and the sworn SURVEY is correct, and no result or disclosure is weakened. This is a latent defect in code and tests: minor, not major.

verdicts.reason:
The omission is real and I reproduced it. The pass-4 protocol requires the record to carry "the conjunction's status". The inherited 2026-09-13 rule gives C6 its own status: RETIRED if one READ source RETIRES or OCCUPIES all of C2-C5, otherwise the weakest of C1-C5. Passes 1, 2 and 3 each wrote a top-level `conjunction` object. The pass-4 builder has no such step, and the pass-4 record has no `conjunction` key and no C6.

I tried to refute it. The strongest defence reads protocol line 137 ("The conjunction's status and the surviving sentence, or RETIRED, or UNLICENSED") as if `sentence.status` (SURVIVES_WITHOUT_C5) were the conjunction's status. The line's own wording lets you read it that way. But the inherited rule gives C6 a separate four-value status, and passes 1-3 recorded it apart from the sentence status. So that reading does not hold up under the earlier precedent, and the omission stands.

The severity is overstated, though:
- **Nothing flips.** Under the rule C6 is RETIRED, because C3 and C4b are RETIRED. That can be worked out from clause statuses the record already carries, and it is the same value passes 1-3 recorded.
- **The empty list was never computed.** `one_source_does_all` is trivially empty. No pass-4 source lists more than one clause under `might_occupy`, and pass 3 hard-coded that list as [] anyway.
- **No sworn or public sentence is affected.** The SURVEY never says the record carries a conjunction status, and the licensed sentence depends on the sentence rule, not on C6.
- **The value carries little.** C6 has read RETIRED in every pass while the sentence survived.

This is an incomplete record against a "must record" item, not a weakened result or disclosure. Minor.

findings.title: The 94 'leads not scored' include 22 entries that are sources already listed and scored, several of them duplicates
findings.claim: leads_not_scored is the exact-string union of readers' lead strings and below-cap titles. It never removes works that are sources in passes 1-4, and never merges the same work cited in different formats. At least 22 of the 94 name listed sources, some of them scored in this pass (B01 twice, B22 twice, B10, B24, A03, A05, A09). Others are S11 four times, S16 four times, S19, L01 twice, L02 and L06. The sworn count of unscored leads is inflated.

verdicts.reason:
The facts hold. papers/plates/build_sand_survey_pass4.py lines 317-318 build leads_not_scored as a plain set of the readers' lead strings plus the below-cap titles. It does not remove works that are already sources and does not merge the same work cited in different formats. The record's list of 94 contains leads for works scored in this very pass (A03, A05, A09, B01, B10, B22, B24), for sources from earlier passes (S11, S16, S19, L01, L02, L06), and the same work several times over.

The severity is overstated, for three reasons.
(1) This is the lab's own recording convention, and the frozen protocol already accounts for it. Pass 3's sworn count of 11 leads also included two works that were already sources: Chen, Zaharia & Zou (p1:S11) and Pineau et al. (p1:S18). The pass 4 protocol's Part A says "The nine unscored leads of pass 3 that are not already sources", which is 11 minus 2. So under the frozen rules, leads_not_scored is a raw list and the filtering happens when the next pass builds its list. No frozen rule requires de-duplication.
(2) The sworn sentence "94 leads are recorded unscored" is true of the field its pointer names (#/n_leads_not_scored = 94 = len(leads_not_scored)).
(3) The count errs in the conservative direction. It appears under "what this survey does not do" as a reason the search is not exhaustive, so it makes the survey look less complete, never more. No status or sentence flips.

It is still a real defect worth a note. The duplicates are new in pass 4 (pass 3 had none). The SURVEY says "108 distinct works" for the search (line 23) but gives no such qualifier for the leads. And the public next-step line "Read the 94 recorded leads" (REPORT line 548, PR comment line 66) points at entries that were already read in this pass. So this is minor: an imprecise disclosure that needs a distinct-work count beside it, not a false sworn statement.

findings.title: UNPRICED C5 is deleted and the sentence licensed, although rule 1 makes C5's status decide the whole sentence
findings.claim: Rule 2 literally allows deleting an UNPRICED clause, and the builder does. But rule 1 makes a RETIRED C5 retire the sentence, and 'UNPRICED is never read as free'. The unfetchable candidate B23 therefore leaves the sentence's own RETIRED-or-not status unchecked. Pass 4 closed this gap for C4a (UNLICENSED) but not for C5, and the SURVEY does not disclose that the licensed sentence depends on B23 not retiring C5.
findings.evidence:

Builder lines 268-291.

The record: /sentence/status = SURVIVES_WITHOUT_C5; /sources/B23/status = UNFETCHABLE with might_occupy ['C5'].

SURVEY lines 91-94 and 144-146.
findings.suggested_repair: Disclose that under rule 1 the sentence's survival rests on an unchecked C5 candidate. Settle the C5 analogue of UNLICENSED in the next protocol.

verdicts.reason: The defect is real, but it is narrower than the finding says. The builder and the record are correct under the frozen rules. Sentence rule 1 applies only when C5's status is RETIRED. The status rule lets only a READ source retire a clause, so B23 (unfetchable) makes C5 UNPRICED, not RETIRED. The pass-4 protocol planned for C5 becoming UNPRICED (line 25). It added UNLICENSED for C4a alone (lines 63-66) and says the rules hold 'amended only as below'. So the builder lines 268-291, /clauses/C5/status and /sentence/status do not break any frozen rule, and they are not a blocker. What I did reproduce is a gap in what the documents say. Under rule 1, B23 is a listed, unchecked C5 candidate, and if read it could retire the whole sentence, not just the bounty clause. The SURVEY warns that C4a could retire the sentence (line 123) but gives no such warning for C5 (lines 91-94, 127-146). The REPORT addendum and the PR comment go further. They describe the Science article as blocking only the bounty clause ('cannot be said until the Science article is read'; 'Do not use the bounty clause until the Science article is read'). That leaves out its possible effect on the whole sentence. In practice the risk is small: B23 is a news piece titled on paying for errors in published papers, and the three sister sources about ERROR (B12, B16, B24) were all coded OCCUPIES. Minor is the right severity. The repair should be a disclosure, not a change to the builder.

findings.title: The SKIMMED path is stricter than the frozen rule, and skimmed OCCUPIES verdicts are not marked 'from abstract'
findings.claim: The frozen rule lets a SKIMMED source be SILENT or OCCUPIES from abstract, and makes a clause UNPRICED only through an UNFETCHABLE (or, in pass 4, a DISPUTED) source. The builder turns a skimmed all-five coding, or a skimmed RETIRES, into UNCHECKABLE and the clause into UNPRICED, which makes the sentence UNLICENSED. It also turns an UNSCORED verdict into UNPRICED. Meanwhile the landing-page OCCUPIES verdicts (B04, B05, B07) carry no 'from abstract' mark and are counted in the SURVEY's 'Seven sources keep hash chains'.
findings.evidence:

Harness case F (X1 in the scope file, coded all five and confirmed; X2 READ at distance 1): X1 UNCHECKABLE; clauses {'C4a': 'UNPRICED'}; sentence UNLICENSED.

The record: /sources/B04/verdicts/C2 = {verdict: OCCUPIES, ...} with no scope mark in the verdict.

SURVEY lines 88-89.
findings.suggested_repair: Record a skimmed RETIRES as OCCUPIES from abstract under the frozen rule, or amend the protocol first. Tag verdicts from SKIMMED sources 'from abstract', and say so where they are counted.

verdicts.reason:
I confirmed the first half by running it myself. The frozen rule (PROTOCOL_sand_prior_art_2026_09_13.md lines 48-51) allows a SKIMMED source only SILENT or OCCUPIES from abstract. Under that rule a clause becomes UNPRICED only through an UNFETCHABLE candidate, and pass 4 adds DISPUTED. The builder does something else: a SKIMMED all-five coding, or a SKIMMED C2/C5 RETIRES, becomes UNCHECKABLE (lines 195-196 and 208-209). Lines 235-236 then make the clause UNPRICED, and C4a UNPRICED makes the sentence UNLICENSED. The frozen rule would record OCCUPIES and leave the sentence standing. Lines 235-236 also turn UNSCORED into UNPRICED. The protocol never defines UNSCORED, so that part is gap-filling rather than a clear breach. The builder docstring (lines 22-24) and tests state this behaviour openly, yet the docstring says it does 'nothing the protocol does not say'.

The defect is latent. The committed record has no uncheckable or unscored source for C2 or C4a. The only UNCHECKABLE is B23 on C5, which is UNFETCHABLE and handled correctly. No reader coded all five on B04, B05 or B07. So no status or sentence in the record is wrong, and minor is the right severity.

The second half is mostly wrong. The C2 verdict entries for B04, B05 and B07 do say 'from abstract' in their own reason field. B04 and B05 say 'so this is coded from the abstract alone'. B07 says 'only the journal landing page and abstract were available'. The sources also carry status SKIMMED and a skimmed_reason, and SURVEY lines 42-47 disclose the three landing pages. What is really missing is only a structured tag, and a note at SURVEY line 88 where the seven are counted. One thing I noticed but did not score here: B07's own reason says 'the abstract does not state that entries are chained'. That is in tension with 'Seven sources keep hash chains' at SURVEY line 88.

findings.title: Rules not in the protocol: the tie-break by id picks the E4 neighbour, and a fallback 'at most three' is invented
findings.claim: The protocol names 'the listed source' per element and gives no tie-break or fallback, yet the docstring says the builder does 'nothing the protocol does not say'. B14 and B22 tie at distance one on E4. The lexicographic id order names B14 ('Karvonen et al.') in the sentence, although the margin record shows B22 is the source with an all-five blind reading. The fallback when no distance-one source exists (up to three sources at the smallest distance) appears nowhere in the protocol.

findings.suggested_repair: Freeze a tie rule and a fallback in the next protocol, or name every source tied at distance one; the protocol allows five names. Remove 'nothing the protocol does not say' from the docstring.

verdicts.reason: The core defect is real and I reproduced it. The builder's docstring says it does "nothing the protocol does not say", but it adds three rules the frozen protocol does not contain. (1) It orders by pass, pass 4 before pass 3, although the protocol says "from any pass". (2) It breaks ties by lower id. (3) When no source anywhere is at distance one, it falls back to up to three sources at the smallest distance. The protocol instead says a name is given only "if such a source exists", which means no name at all. Two parts of the finding are overstated. First, that B22 has an all-five margin reading does not make B14 the wrong choice under the frozen rules. The first reading and the record code B22 at distance 1, and the sworn SURVEY (lines 119-120) says the margin check "changes no status". Naming either source fits "the listed source". Second, the tie is disclosed, not hidden. The record lists at_distance_one_by_element/E4 = [B14, B22] and states the lower-id rule, and the sworn SURVEY (lines 76-79) names Chauvin et al. as tied with DiFR. The tie-break was committed in 450265ff, before the Part B list existed (178c2d6a), so it was not picked with B14 or B22 in view. The fallback never ran in this record: named_in_sentence comes from by_element and is not empty. No sworn or public sentence is false, and no status changes. What is wrong is the builder's statement that it follows the protocol and nothing else, plus rules no one froze. That is minor, as claimed.

There is no tie-break or fallback. The only tie rule anywhere in the protocol is for the search cap (line 125). The inherited protocols have none for neighbours either (checked with Select-String for tie|nearest|lower id|at most).

build_sand_survey_pass4.py line 13 says "per PROTOCOL..., and nothing the protocol does not say". Lines 34-36 of the docstring: "pass 4's coding first ... and, if no source anywhere is at distance one, the sources at the smallest distance (at most three)". Line 257: at1.sort(key=lambda p: (-p["pass"], p["id"])). Lines 260-262: nearest_overall = sorted(...)[:3]; named = [by_element...] or nearest_overall. Line 265 is the rule string, which states "then the lower id ... at most three".

findings.title: Neighbour phrases can be garbled, and unknown verdict words are silently ignored
findings.claim: html.unescape also decodes entity prefixes that lack a semicolon ('&not' becomes '¬'). bare() cuts a phrase at its first ' without', dropping content. A verdict word outside the RETIRES/OCCUPIES/SILENT vocabulary (for example 'RETIRED') falls into no bucket, so the clause stays OCCUPIED with no error. The workflow schema enforces the enum, but the builder does not.
findings.evidence:

Harness case H/I sentence: 'where Doe et al. audit served models, without an interval on the comparison; where Smith ¬es drift in a served model ...'. The inputs were 'Doe et al. audit served models without access to weights against a same-weights null floor' and 'Smith &notes drift ...'.

Harness case G (C5 verdict 'RETIRED'): C5 pass4 buckets all empty; C5 OCCUPIED; sentence SURVIVES.
findings.suggested_repair: Unescape only entities that end in a semicolon. Strip only a trailing ', without …' clause. Assert that every verdict is in the allowed vocabulary.

verdicts.reason: I reproduced all three mechanisms against build_sand_survey_pass4.py at HEAD 3060ffd2. None of them touches the committed record or the sworn sentence, so they are latent robustness defects. Minor is the right severity, not overstated. (1) html.unescape decodes named entities that lack a semicolon, so '&notes' becomes '¬es'. (2) bare() at line 279 cuts at the first ' without' anywhere in a phrase, not only a trailing ', without' clause. The only test for it (test_a_phrase_that_already_says_without_is_not_doubled, line 159) covers just the trailing case. (3) Lines 225-238 drop any verdict word outside RETIRES/OCCUPIES/SILENT/DISPUTED/UNCHECKABLE/UNSCORED from every bucket, and nothing asserts on it. Such a word also skips the confirmation branch at line 201, and line 216's setdefault only fills clauses that are missing, so the clause can end OCCUPIED with exit code 0. The read_pass4.js schema enforces the enum upstream, but the builder does not check it. Why it is not higher: every committed reader verdict is in the vocabulary. No committed phrase has an '&' entity that unescape changes. The one phrase containing ' without' is pass3:L05, and there the cut is exactly the intended trailing-clause strip. A rebuild from the committed inputs is byte-identical in content to the committed record, so no status or sentence is wrong under the frozen rules.

findings.title: The C2 neighbour is hardcoded from pass 1, and the 'nearer' flags the protocol says are recorded were never collected
findings.claim: The pass-4 protocol lets this pass name nearer neighbours, and says readers' 'nearer' flags are recorded. The reader schema has no nearer field, and the builder hardcodes CT and Rekor as C2's neighbour (P3_PARTS) whatever pass 4 found. B08's reader writes that an auditor re-derives the chain heads and digests from bytes, which is at least a candidate nearer than certificate logs. Neither the builder nor the record addresses nearness for C2.
findings.evidence:
PROTOCOL pass4 lines 25-26 and 73. PROTOCOL_2026_09_13 rule 3, line 63.

prompts/read_pass4.js SCHEMA (lines 12-31): verdict keys clause/verdict/object/reason/neighbour_phrase/elements only.

Builder lines 51-56 and 282-283.

The record: /clauses/C2/nearest = ['S07','S08'] (inherited). /sources/B08/verdicts/C2/object: '...an auditor re-derives the chain heads and delta digests'.
findings.suggested_repair: State in the record that C2's and C5's neighbours were not re-evaluated and that no nearer flags were collected. Or add a counted or flagged nearness step for C2 and C5 in the next protocol.

verdicts.reason: I reproduced both parts. (1) Protocol pass 4 line 73 says readers' "nearer" flags "are recorded". Pass 3 did collect them (build_sand_survey_pass3.py:125-126, field `nearer_than_pass2_neighbour`), but pass 4's reader schema dropped the field. No key containing "nearer" appears in any pass-4 readings file, and the only nearer keys in the record are inherited from pass 3. So the flags the protocol says are recorded were never collected. (2) Protocol lines 25-26 let this pass "name nearer neighbours", and inherited sentence rule 3 (PROTOCOL_2026_09_13 line 63) wants the "nearest neighbour named". Pass 4 dropped the only nearness step it had for C2 and C5, the reader flag, and put a counting rule in its place for C4a only. The reader prompt never shows readers C2's current neighbours (CT/Rekor), so nobody could judge nearness. The builder copies P3_PARTS["C2"] into the sentence whenever C2 is OCCUPIED (lines 53, 282-283), even though pass 4 added seven new C2 OCCUPIES sources (B03-B08, B25). /clauses/C2/nearest stays ["S07","S08"] from pass 1. Why I did not refute it: this is a real gap between protocol and implementation, and the record does not disclose it. The builder docstring (line 32, "pass 3's wording for C1, C2 and C5") is the only place it is stated. Why it is not more severe: B08 is not clearly nearer than CT/Rekor. Its own reader calls it "the same mechanism applied to a different object", and CT is also described as chaining non-verdicts. B03 and B06 chain verdicts but never re-derive them. The frozen rules define no nearness count for C2, and the "nearer flags" sentence sits in the C4a section. So no sworn sentence or status is shown false. C5 is UNPRICED and deleted from the sentence, so its neighbour does not matter.

findings.title: Four of 25 list slots come from an unfrozen null-year rule that the SURVEY calls 'the frozen tie-break'
findings.claim: The cap was applied with every missing year treated as year 0 (ranked oldest). The frozen rule does not say this. The protocol also requires a year for every result, yet all 106 web results were recorded with year null, including works whose returned title or URL states a year. The SURVEY blames the outcome on 'the frozen tie-break by later year'. Four of the 25 slots depend on this choice.
findings.evidence:
1) papers/plates/sand_survey_pass4_inputs/prompts/search_pass4_run2.js:200 sorts with `((y.year || 0) - (x.year || 0))`, and line 55 tells the web agent 'year null unless the tool's text states them'.
2) PROTOCOL_sand_prior_art_pass4_2026_09_15.md, Part B: 'Every result is recorded with the engine, the query, its rank, its title, authors, year, link and, where the engine returns one, its abstract.' Only the abstract is conditional.
3) search_record.json#/engine_returns/web/notes: 'year null (no per-result authorship or year stated)'. All 25 web-only entered works have year null (rank.js output).
4) The raw web text does state years for listed works. survey4\search\web\Q01.md has B01's link 'https://mlanthology.org/iclr/2025/gao2025iclr-model/'. web\Q03.md has B09's title 'An Auditing Test to Detect Behavioral Shift in Language ModelsThis work was published at ICLR 2025.' web\Q08.md has B19's title 'LLM Model Drift Detection 2026: ...'.
5) Sensitivity (redteam_pass4\rank.js): using the year encoded in each arXiv id instead of null moves four works into the list, below-cap ranks 26 (2601.19934), 32 (2506.09501), 33 (2511.02620) and 34 (2504.12335, 'You've Changed: Detecting Modification of Black-Box Large Language Models'). It moves B19, B21, B23 and B24 out.
6) SURVEY_sand_neighbours_pass4_2026_09_14.md lines 31-33: 'The web engine answered all twelve but gives no year, so the frozen tie-break by later year ranked every dated work above every undated one at equal hit counts.' The effect is disclosed, but the cause is attributed to the frozen rule when it was an implementation choice.
findings.suggested_repair: Add a CORRECTION beside the SURVEY stating: (a) ranking missing years last was the workflow's choice, not the protocol's; (b) the protocol's 'year for every result' was not met for the web engine; (c) the four in and four out that recorded years (from arXiv ids or venue URLs) would produce. The next protocol should freeze how a missing year is handled and where a year may be taken from.

verdicts.reason: The core defect holds. The frozen protocol never says how a missing year is ranked. The workflow treated every missing year as 0 (the oldest), so all 26 undated works that one pair returned sort below every dated work. The sworn SURVEY calls this 'the frozen tie-break by later year', which presents a workflow choice as the protocol's rule. Nothing else discloses the choice: the record, the report addendum and the PR comment have no rule for a null year. Which works make the list does depend on it. With a missing year ranked newest instead, six of the 25 slots swap: the five 2026 intrusion-detection papers and AuditableLLM leave. Two parts of the finding are overstated. (1) The figure 'four slots' holds only if years are taken from arXiv ids, which neither the protocol nor the prompt allows. Taking only the years the tool's text states, which is the prompt's own rule, changes nothing: 0 in, 0 out. The fair statement is 'between 0 and 6 slots, depending on the unfrozen null-year handling and where years may be taken from'. (2) The claim that 'year for every result' was breached is weak. The WebSearch tool returns no year for each result, the search agent was told not to open results, and the SURVEY already says the web engine 'gives no year'. The only real slip is that the web agent left the year null where the returned title states one (B09 'published at ICLR 2025', B19 '2026'), and that does not change membership. The effect (dated works above undated ones, undated works pushed below the cap) is disclosed, and no status is shown to flip. So this weakens the disclosure without falsifying the result: major, not blocker. It is arguably minor, because the effect itself is disclosed.

verdicts.reason:
I reproduced it. The frozen cap rule (PROTOCOL_sand_prior_art_pass4_2026_09_15.md:125-127) says ties are 'broken by the later year, then by title'. It says nothing about a result that has no year. The workflow ranked every missing year as year 0. That line is already in search_pass4_run1.js:135 and search_pass4_run2.js:200, so it was set before any result was seen, but it appears nowhere in the protocol, in search_record.json's rank_rule or in the SURVEY. The SURVEY (lines 31-33) says 'the frozen tie-break by later year ranked every dated work above every undated one'. Membership of the list depends on this choice. Ranking undated works first swaps six works. Taking the year from arXiv ids swaps exactly the four the finding names. The finding also understates the consequence. Two of the four works pushed out are B23 and B24. B23 (UNFETCHABLE, C5 UNCHECKABLE) is the only uncheckable C5 source, which makes C5 UNPRICED and puts the sentence at SURVIVES_WITHOUT_C5. So the public headline 'the bounty clause out of the sentence' rests on this unfrozen choice. I rate it major, not blocker: under a silent rule some choice had to be made, dated-before-undated is a defensible one, and the effect is disclosed. The defect is the misattribution plus a sensitivity nobody reported.

findings.title: Screener inclusions whose own reasons say the rule was not met or not applied, while matching works were excluded
findings.claim: Under 'either includes', a single screener's decision decides a slot. At least three list slots rest on a decision whose own reason concedes the rule was not met or was deferred, and each has a matching counterpart that was excluded. Removing B08 and B21 alone would bring below-cap ranks 26 and 27 into the list. Including the matching IoT provenance work (2 pairs, 2026) would rank it third and push B25 out. No clause status flips: C2 stays occupied by B03-B07 and B25, and C4a stays at distance one via B01, B14 and B22.
findings.evidence:
All quotes are from search_record.json.
1) B08 AuditableLLM. screener1: include=false, 'logs model updates, not evaluation results or verdicts'. screener2: include=true, 'close enough to (c) that a thin reading should not exclude it'. The abstract is not thin: it is a full paragraph saying it 'records each update as a hash-chain-backed, tamper-evident audit trail'. By contrast, excluded work 't:tamper evident data and model provenance for iot...' (n_engine_query_pairs 2, year 2026) was excluded by both screeners for recording 'hashes and metadata of data, preprocessing outputs, and trained models', which is the same kind of artifact log.
2) B21 'LLMs don't stand still: How to monitor and trust the models powering your AI'. screener1: 'not a paper'. screener2: include=true, 'with no abstract, its document type is left for the next step'. The protocol has no next screening step. By contrast, 'What Is LLM Behavioral Drift and Why Should You Monitor It?' was excluded as not a paper by both screeners.
3) B13 'Defeating Nondeterminism in LLM Inference: Theory to Deterministic Code Edits' (morphllm.com blog). screener2 included it as 'a derivative rather than the Thinking Machines source'. The same screener role excluded 'Explained: Defeating Nondeterminism in LLM Inference' as 'already scored: ... (Thinking Machines)'.
4) These slots count in the record: sand_prior_art_survey_pass4_2026_09_14.json codes B08 as C2 OCCUPIES and C4a OCCUPIES at distance 4, B21 as C4a OCCUPIES at distance 4, and B13 as C4a SILENT.
affected: papers/plates/sand_survey_pass4_inputs/search_record.json#/excluded (Tamper-Evident Data and Model Provenance for IoT; What Is LLM Behavioral Drift; Explained: Defeating Nondeterminism)
findings.suggested_repair: Record these inconsistencies in the CORRECTION or in the next pass's ledger, listing the below-cap works each wrongly admitted slot displaced. For the next protocol: screeners must not defer the document-type test and must not include on 'close enough' when a full abstract is present; add a reconciliation step for split decisions.

verdicts.reason:
I reproduced the core defect for B08 and B21. For B13 the finding overreaches, and I think "major" overstates it.

**B08.** One screener agent, screen:b0:s2, used in the recorded run starting 22:10:59, made three of the decisions in question:
- It included AuditableLLM as "close enough to (c) that a thin reading should not exclude it". The abstract it was shown is a full paragraph, so the committed prompt's leniency for thin snippets did not apply.
- In the same batch it excluded the IoT provenance work for logging artifacts rather than verdicts, which is the same kind of object.
- It also included B21 while saying the document type "is left for the next step". The protocol and prompt make not-a-paper an exclusion, and there is no next screening step.

**The arithmetic holds.** I re-ranked under the frozen rule:
- Without B08 and B21, below-cap ranks 26 (arXiv 2601.19934, which both screeners included) and 27 enter the list.
- With the IoT work added (2 pairs, 2026), it ranks 3 and QCIVET (B25) falls to 26.

**Where it is weaker or overstated.**
- **B13:** screener2's reason does not admit the rule was unmet. It claims clause (b) and says it is not the already-scored source. The same agent excluding "Explained:" as a restatement is a judgement a reader can defend. B13 is also coded SILENT, so it moves nothing.
- **B21's counterpart:** "What Is LLM Behavioral Drift" was decided by different agents (batch b1), not by the agent that included B21.
- **The record follows the frozen rules.** The protocol says "a result enters when either includes it", and the order matches the record. No status, nearest-neighbour name (C2: S07, S08; C4a: S12, S16, L03, L06, L08) or sworn statement changes. "Two screeners decided every work" is true.
- **B08 held up on full reading:** it is a legitimate C2 neighbour ("same mechanism applied to a different object").

So the defect is real screener error in two decisions, recorded faithfully. It costs two of 25 slots and is not disclosed. It does not weaken a stated result: minor, not major.
verdicts.evidence:
1) search_record.json list_b B08: screener1 include=false ("logs model updates, not evaluation results or verdicts"); screener2 include=true ("close enough to (c) that a thin reading should not exclude it"). The B08 abstract in the record is about 1,300 characters and the prompt passes up to 1,500. The prompt (prompts/search_pass4_run2.js line 74) says: "Doubt about (a)-(d) from a thin snippet is not a reason to exclude when the title itself plainly fits".

2) B21: screener2 says "with no abstract, its document type is left for the next step". The same prompt line says to exclude "when it is not a paper, report or standing programme page". The fetched URL is catchpoint.com/blog, and the record's notes call it a "Vendor marketing blog".

3) Agent attribution: scratchpad/redteam_pass4/screen_agents.py parses the StructuredOutput of each screen agent in wf_fdf4dfce-ffd.
- Agent a258c318c54ef82ec (screen:b0:s2, 22:10:59 to 22:11:59) returned auditablellm include=True, llms-don't-stand-still include=True and IoT provenance include=False, all matching the record.
- Agent acabef770667a628c (b1:s2) returned B13 include=True and "Explained" include=False.
- "What Is LLM Behavioral Drift" was decided in batch b1, not b0.

4) scratchpad/redteam_pass4/rerank.py: "recomputed order matches record: True".
- Without B08 and B21, positions 24 and 25 are "Quantifying non-deterministic drift in large language models" and "Tamper-proof Logs for AI Inference Models".
- With IoT added (pairs=2, year=2026), it sits at position 3 and QCIVET drops to 26.

5) No status or name flips. sand_prior_art_survey_pass4_2026_09_14.json /clauses: C2 nearest [S07, S08]; C4a nearest [S12, S16, L03, L06, L08]. B08 is C2 OCCUPIES with the object "An append-only SHA-256 hash chain of per-step LLM update events", B21 is C4a OCCUPIES at distance 4, and B13 is C4a SILENT.

6) The protocol's inclusion rule says "a result enters when either includes it". The SURVEY says "Two screeners decided every work" (true). Its "what the lab got wrong" section does not mention split or self-contradicting screener decisions.

verdicts.reason:
I reproduced the core of the finding. The frozen protocol and the screener prompt both require a screener to exclude a work that is not a paper, report or standing programme page. The "thin snippet" allowance covers only doubt about rules (a) to (d), and only when the title plainly fits. One screener-2 agent broke this twice. For B21 it left the document-type test "for the next step", and the protocol has no next step. For B08 it included the work as "close enough to (c)" although the full abstract describes a log of model updates, not of evaluation results or verdicts. In the same batch, the same agent excluded the IoT provenance work, whose abstract describes the same kind of artifact log. Because the list is capped at 25, each wrong inclusion pushes out a work both screeners included. Removing B21 alone brings in rank 26, arXiv 2601.19934 "Quantifying non-deterministic drift in large language models", which is on topic for C4a. The survey and report do not disclose that any screen decision misapplied the rule.

Parts of the claim are overstated:
(1) Excluding the IoT work was correct under rule (c). The proper repair is to drop B08, not to add the IoT work, so the "IoT would rank third and push B25 out" scenario is not what the rules call for.
(2) B08 is borderline. The reader coded it C2 OCCUPIES on the full text, so its inclusion did no harm to that clause.
(3) B13 is the weakest item. Screeners saw only a cleaned title, with " | Morph" removed and no URL. A derivative page is not "another version or edition" of the Thinking Machines post, so "not already scored" follows the rule. The agent's own document-type test was not applied there, though.

No sworn sentence and no clause status changes, as the finding says. I keep the severity at major, not blocker: a vendor blog took a list slot from an arXiv paper both screeners included, and that paper bears on C4a's rarest element (E3, true in 3 sources). The displaced works stay recorded as leads.

findings.title: SURVEY says the record 'keeps every response's hash'; the only responses showing Q11/Q12 had no match were overwritten and are unhashed
findings.claim: The run-1 Semantic Scholar script wrote every try of a query to the same file, so each raw file holds only its last try. For Q11 and Q12 the last try was a 429. The HTTP 200 {"total": 0} responses behind 'two more were answered with no match' were therefore overwritten and have no hash in the record. The claim rests on an agent's notes and an uncommitted background log. So does the six-failure count, which excludes Q11 and Q12 on that basis.
findings.evidence:
1) survey4\s2_run.py runs, for each try: curl ... "-o", path, with path = Q11.json, the same file every try.
2) survey4\search\s2\Q11.json and Q12.json (174 bytes each; hashes match search_record.json#/raw_files) both contain {"message": "Too Many Requests...", "code": "429"}.
3) tasks\bclrt1vp2.output, the run-1 script's log, which is not in the record: 'Q11 try 1 failed: http 200 body {"total": 0' and 'Q12 try 4 failed: http 200 body {"total": 0'. The same log shows first-try 429s for Q03, Q08 and Q09 that were also overwritten.
4) search_record.json#/engine_returns/s2/notes: 'each of their raw files holds the last 429 body'.
5) SURVEY_sand_neighbours_pass4_2026_09_14.md lines 26-27: '`sand_survey_pass4_inputs/search_record.json` keeps every response's hash'. Line 30: 'two more were answered with no match'.
6) My re-send of Q11/Q12 at 2026-09-15T00:37-00:40Z (redteam_pass4\s2_probe.py) got HTTP 429 on every try, so it could not check the claim.
findings.suggested_repair: The CORRECTION should say the record hashes only the last response per query of the first Semantic Scholar run. It should also say the answered-with-no-match status rests on the run-1 script's log, which should be committed or hashed if still available (tasks\bclrt1vp2.output). Future engine scripts should save every try to its own file, as retry_one.py already does.

verdicts.reason: The overwrite is real: s2/Q11.json and s2/Q12.json hold only the last 429 body. But the finding's main claim is wrong. It says the HTTP 200 {"total": 0} answers have no hash in the record and rest only on an agent's notes and an uncommitted background log (tasks\bclrt1vp2.output). In fact the run-1 script also saves its full per-try log inside s2_parsed.json, and that log records both 200 bodies. s2_parsed.json is hashed in search_record.json#/raw_files. I recomputed its sha256 and it matches. So the no-match status for Q11/Q12, and the six-failure count that leaves them out, rest on a file whose hash the record keeps. They do not rest on the background log. The record also discloses the overwrite and the retry-after-200 in engine_returns/s2/notes and failures. The SURVEY itself says, at lines 157-158, that the first prompt "re-sent two queries that had already been answered." What is left is a wording point. "keeps every response's hash" is loose if "response" means every HTTP try: run-1 try bytes and the arXiv run-1 empty 301 files were overwritten. The record states each of those in its notes, and it flips no status, count or sentence. At most that is minor, not major.
verdicts.evidence:
1) survey4\s2_run.py: out = {"results","failures","raw_files","log"}; every failed try appends "%s try %d failed: %s" to out["log"]; at the end, json.dump(out, open(os.path.join(D, "..", "s2_parsed.json"), "w")). The log is written into s2_parsed.json.
2) Command: python hashlib over survey4\search\s2_parsed.json gave 59037 bytes, sha256 3425360781eed29b4bcc39dc52ceaa559a3313366c07291501b0c5838589cba0. This matches search_record.json#/raw_files entry {"file": "s2_parsed.json", "bytes": 59037, "sha256": "3425360781...cba0"}.
3) s2_parsed.json /log contains "Q11 try 1 failed: http 200 body {\"total\": 0, \"offset\": 0}" and "Q12 try 4 failed: http 200 body {\"total\": 0, \"offset\": 0}". The body is 26 chars, under the script's [:200] cut, so it is complete. It is re-serialized JSON, not the raw bytes.
4) s2/Q11.json and s2/Q12.json are each 174 bytes with sha256 65ab993d... (the 429 body), matching raw_files. So the overwrite part is true.
5) search_record.json#/engine_returns/s2/notes discloses: "each of their raw files holds the last 429 body. Q11 on try 1 and Q12 on try 4 got HTTP 200 with {\"total\": 0, \"offset\": 0}". #/engine_returns/s2/failures gives the per-try detail for Q11 and Q12. #/searches/1/answered_empty is ["Q11","Q12"]. #/searches/1/failures lists six queries (Q01, Q02, Q04, Q06, Q07, Q10), all 5/5 429 in the s2_retry run, with every try hashed (s2_retry/Qnn.tryN.json). build_sand_survey_pass4.py:313 counts search_failures from those entries, giving 6.
6) SURVEY_sand_neighbours_pass4_2026_09_14.md lines 157-158: "The first Semantic Scholar prompt treated a response with no match as unanswered, and re-sent two queries that had already been answered." This is disclosed in the sworn text.
7) Protocol pass4 lines 132-141 require, for each query result, the engine, query, rank and what was returned, plus the sha256 of fetched source bytes. They set no rule that every HTTP try's raw bytes be hashed as its own file, so no frozen rule is broken.

verdicts.reason: I could not refute two of the facts. s2_run.py writes every try to the same QNN.json. The committed hashes for s2/Q11.json and s2/Q12.json both match the 174-byte 429 body. But the central claim fails. The finding says the HTTP 200 {"total": 0} answers for Q11 and Q12 "rest on an agent's notes and an uncommitted background log" that "is not in the record". That is wrong. s2_run.py adds every try, with its HTTP code and body, to out["log"] and saves that log in search/s2_parsed.json. That file is hashed in search_record.json#/raw_files (59037 bytes, sha256 3425360781…cba0), and the hash matches the file on disk. Its log holds both 200 answers word for word. So answered_empty rests on a hashed file, with the same standing as every other uncommitted raw response. The protocol says raw texts are not committed and their sha256 are. That covers every search input the same way, so this is not a special gap. The six-failure count follows from that hashed log, so it is not left without evidence either. What remains is a wording nit. The hash for a run-1 retry covers the log entry that holds its body, not the raw bytes of that response, so "keeps every response's hash" is loose. That is minor at most, and it does not weaken any disclosure or change any status. The suggested repair, committing or hashing tasks\bclrt1vp2.output, is already done in effect, because the same log is hashed as s2_parsed.json.
verdicts.evidence:
1) scratchpad\survey4\s2_run.py: for each try it runs `out["log"].append("%s try %d failed: %s" % (qid, t + 1, err))` with err = "http %s body %s" % (code, json.dumps(j)[:200]). At the end it runs `json.dump(out, open(os.path.join(D, "..", "s2_parsed.json"), "w", ...))`. So every run-1 response's code and body goes into s2_parsed.json.
2) `sha256sum scratchpad/survey4/search/s2_parsed.json` gives 3425360781eed29b4bcc39dc52ceaa559a3313366c07291501b0c5838589cba0. That equals the search_record.json#/raw_files entry {"file": "s2_parsed.json", "bytes": 59037, "sha256": "3425360781…cba0"}. record_search.py line 9 says each saved response "is hashed into the record by path, size and sha256".
3) Loading s2_parsed.json["log"] prints "Q11 try 1 failed: http 200 body {\"total\": 0, \"offset\": 0}" and "Q12 try 4 failed: http 200 body {\"total\": 0, \"offset\": 0}". Q11 tries 2-5 and Q12 tries 1-3 and 5 show http 429. The first-try 429s for Q03, Q08 and Q09 are there too. tasks\bclrt1vp2.output carries the same lines, so the log the finding calls "not in the record" is kept in a hashed record file.
4) Reproduced and not disputed: s2/Q11.json and s2/Q12.json are 174 bytes with sha256 65ab993d…a148 (the 429 body), matching raw_files. search_record.json#/searches/1/answered_empty = ["Q11","Q12"], and failures lists six queries (Q01, Q02, Q04, Q06, Q07, Q10), each with five timestamped 429 tries from run 2.
5) SURVEY_sand_neighbours_pass4_2026_09_14.md line 26: "keeps every response's hash" (unsworn prose). Line 30: "two more were answered with no match". The second statement is supported by the hashed s2_parsed.json log. The first is imprecise only because run-1 retries are hashed inside a log file, not one file per response.
6) The pass-4 protocol (PROTOCOL_sand_prior_art_pass4_2026_09_15.md, the "What the survey must record" section) requires hashes of what is not committed. It does not require per-try raw files, so no frozen rule is broken.

findings.title: 'Five 2026 intrusion-detection papers' is wrong: B04 BlockFedX is not an intrusion-detection paper
findings.claim: The SURVEY says the tie-break 'put five 2026 intrusion-detection papers on the list'. Only four of the 2026 Semantic Scholar entries (B03, B05, B06, B07) are intrusion-detection papers. B04 BlockFedX is a cross-domain federated learning system for fraud detection, brain-tumour MRI and plant disease.
findings.evidence:
1) SURVEY_sand_neighbours_pass4_2026_09_14.md lines 32-33: 'That rule put five 2026 intrusion-detection papers on the list'.
2) search_record.json list_b B04 abstract: 'BlockFedX is a cross-domain federated learning system designed to address three simultaneous tasks: credit card fraud detection on tabular data, brain tumour detection on MRI images, and plant disease recognition on leaf images.'
3) Titles of B03, B05, B06 and B07 all name intrusion detection.
findings.suggested_repair: One line in the CORRECTION: four 2026 intrusion-detection papers and one 2026 federated-learning logging system.

verdicts.reason: I reproduced it. The tie-break did put five 2026 works on the list: B03 to B07 each have one hit and year 2026. But only four of them are intrusion-detection papers. B04 BlockFedX is a federated learning system for credit-card fraud, brain-tumour MRI and plant disease. Its "anomaly detection" is a distance test on client model updates, not network intrusion detection. So the count of five is right and the label is wrong for one of the five. I looked for a reading that saves the sentence and found none: B04's record title, abstract and fetched text never use the word "intrusion". The sentence is plain prose, not inside a sworn tag, but it sits in a document whose receipt is committed. It changes no status, verdict or sworn number, so minor is the right severity. No pass-4 CORRECTION exists yet. The phrase also does not appear in the report, the CHANGELOG, the PR comment or the pass-4 protocol, so the SURVEY is the only place to repair.

findings.title: Dedupe: one wrong merge and one missed merge, which cancel out so that 108 happens to be right
findings.claim: The whole-word prefix rule wrongly joined two different web pages into one work. Separately, the arXiv-id regex missed an id in a Bytez URL, so one paper stayed as two works and got opposite screening decisions. Because both errors fall within a single engine-query pair, neither changes any pair count or rank, and they offset each other in the count of 108.
findings.evidence:
1) Wrong merge: search_record.json excluded work key 't:what is ai transparency definition futureagi guide 2026' holds hits web/Q10/r6 'What Is AI Transparency? Definition & FutureAGI Guide (2026)' (futureagi.com) and web/Q10/r9 'What Is AI Transparency? | IBM' (ibm.com/think/topics/ai-transparency). Cause: run2.js:153 joins when one cleaned title of three or more words is a whole-word prefix of another ('what is ai transparency').
2) Missed merge: excluded work key 't:bytez' has url https://bytez.com/docs/arxiv/2504.12335/paper (web/Q03/r10), which is the same paper as below-cap rank 34, arxiv:2504.12335 (web/Q03/r3). Cause: run2.js:126 ARXIV_IN matches 'arxiv:' or 'arxiv ' but not 'arxiv/'. Both screeners excluded 'Bytez' as 'not a paper' and both included rank 34.
3) Related cosmetic defect: B09's recorded title carries the glued text 'Language ModelsThis work was published at ICLR 2025.'
affected: papers/plates/sand_survey_pass4_inputs/search_record.json#/excluded (t:bytez, t:what is ai transparency definition futureagi guide 2026)
findings.suggested_repair: Note both in the next pass's ledger. Accept 'arxiv/<id>' in the id regex, and require the same domain family (or an author match) before joining on a title prefix.

verdicts.reason: I reproduced both dedupe errors by running the code's own regex and title functions, and I checked them against search_record.json and the raw web responses. The frozen pass-4 protocol has no dedupe rule of its own. The code states one (DEDUPE_RULE, run2.js:125, "join results sharing an arXiv identifier (link or title)"), and the code misses its own case. The Bytez link carries 2504.12335 but was not joined. The whole-word prefix step also joined two different web pages: a FutureAGI glossary page and an IBM topic page. No status, pair count or rank changes. The Bytez hit (web|Q03) is a pair that arxiv:2504.12335 already has, so it stays at 1 pair and rank 34. Both FutureAGI and IBM are web|Q10 and both are excluded. The IBM page is a vendor explainer, so it would be excluded as "not a paper" even if screened under its own title. The two errors cancel in the count: 108 - 1 (merge Bytez) + 1 (split IBM) = 108. So the sworn "108 distinct works" still matches what the stated rule intended, as far as these two cases go. I found no disclosure of either case in the pass-4 docs, CHANGELOG, report or PR comment. One gap the finding does not mention: the screeners never saw the IBM result's own title, only the FutureAGI title. That is harmless here. Minor is the right severity; it is not overstated. B09's glued title is the web engine's title copied verbatim ("title_as_returned" in raw Q03.md), so it is cosmetic, as the finding says.
verdicts.evidence:
1) I wrote scratchpad\redteam_pass4\dedupe_check_skeptic1.js, copying ARXIV_IN, arxivId, displayTitle and cleanTitle verbatim from papers/plates/sand_survey_pass4_inputs/prompts/search_pass4_run2.js:126-138, plus the prefix test from line 153. Output:
- "bytez id: null"
- "arxiv pdf id: 2504.12335"
- "ibm clean: \"what is ai transparency\" futureagi clean: \"what is ai transparency definition futureagi guide 2026\""
- "prefix join: true"
ARXIV_IN only matches arxiv.org/(abs|pdf|html)/, /paper(s)/ with a trailing slash, "arxiv:" or "arxiv " and "[". The Bytez URL is https://bytez.com/docs/arxiv/2504.12335/paper: it has "arxiv/" and ends in "/paper" with no slash, so nothing matches.

2) search_record.json, lines 3101-3134: arxiv:2504.12335 has one hit, web Q03 rank 3 (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2504.12335). Both screeners include it as C4a, and it went "below cap, rank 34".
Lines 3917-3950: t:bytez has one hit, web Q03 rank 10 (https://bytez.com/docs/arxiv/2504.12335/paper). Both screeners exclude it as "not a paper".
Lines 5201-5242: t:what is ai transparency definition futureagi guide 2026 has two hits, web Q10 r6 (futureagi.com/glossary/transparency/) and web Q10 r9 "What Is AI Transparency? | IBM" (ibm.com/think/topics/ai-transparency). Both screeners give reasons quoting only the FutureAGI title.

3) Raw web responses in scratchpad\survey4\search\web:
- Q03.md: Bytez is the 10th link and "You've Changed..." (arxiv.org/pdf/2504.12335) is the 3rd.
- Q10.md: the FutureAGI transparency page is the 6th link and the IBM page is the 9th.

4) scratchpad\redteam_pass4\count_check_skeptic1.py output:
- "works with hits: 108 distinct keys: 108 total hits: 133"
- counts.search_distinct = 108, which the SURVEY swears at line 23.
- Fixing both errors gives 108 - 1 + 1 = 108.
- No pair count moves: Bytez's pair web|Q03 duplicates rank 34's pair, and IBM/FutureAGI are both web|Q10 and excluded.

5) grep for bytez, ibm.com and prefix across papers/plates/*.md, papers/chat/REPORT_2026_09_13.md, CHANGELOG.md and pr87_comment_pass4.md found no disclosure of either case.

6) The glued title "An Auditing Test to Detect Behavioral Shift in Language ModelsThis work was published at ICLR 2025." is the web engine's own link title in raw Q03.md. It is carried into search_record.json:2170, list.json:236 and sand_prior_art_survey_pass4_2026_09_14.json:2632.

findings.title: An intermediate Semantic Scholar retry prompt that would have re-sent the answered Q11/Q12 ran but is neither committed nor disclosed

The status does not flip C4a: B11 is at distance 2 and not in the parenthesis.

verdicts.reason:
Reproduced. B11's fetched text (sha256 64886ac5…) is alphaXiv's /abs page for arXiv 2603.19022: a 19-line abstract, then an "AI Overview", citation cards and site chrome. It is not the authors' paper, and B11's own reader said so in the notes. The builder still recorded READ, because fetched_text_scope.json lists only B04, B05 and B07.

The lab's own rule is committed. The scope file's _rule and the builder's docstring (lines 21-22) say a landing page fetched instead of the article's text is SKIMMED whatever its reader shows. The inherited protocol allows a SKIMMED source only SILENT or OCCUPIES 'from abstract'. Applied consistently, B11 is SKIMMED.

Every part of the proof of reading for B11 comes from machine text that is not in the paper:
- the E2 quote;
- the midpoint quote;
- the last-line quote, which is site chrome ('Sign in to save');
- bearing quotes 3 and 4.

Checking against the arXiv PDF found more than the finding reported. The defect does not flip C4a or the sentence: B11 is at distance 2, OCCUPIES either way, and is not in the parenthesis. The paper itself also supports E2 ('a fixed, model-agnostic prompt set'), so no element value changes.

- counts/skimmed: 3 should be 4
- c4a_element_true E1: 15 should be 14

The builder's broader wording ('a landing page fetched instead of the article's text') and the plain meaning of READ cover B11. If a reviewer holds that only the frozen protocol text counts, this could be graded major. Under the lab's rubric, where a wrong record status or a false sworn number is a blocker, it stands as a blocker.

verdicts.reason:
The facts check out: the margin prompt was written after the first build, and it restates E3, E4 and E5. The defect built on those facts does not hold up.

1. The restatement is the frozen protocol's own wording. It is not stricter than the protocol. The E4 text matches the protocol almost word for word. The E5 text drops the protocol's exclusions ("not from sampled text, extracted answers or hard labels alone"), so if anything it is looser. Both prompts tell readers to read the full protocol and use only its definitions.
2. There is no sign that the wording pushed readers. The first B-run readers had no restatement (read_pass4.js), and they coded E4 false on B14 and B22 for the same reasons the margin readers later gave: "alpha is never given a value", "no p-value is reported", "the CIs bound AUC rather than the compared statistic S", "12-standard-deviation threshold with no stated level". So the "uptake" quotes come from the protocol, not from the added line. E3 and E5 got the same restatement, yet all 8 B14/B22 margin readers coded both true, and all 4 B01 readers coded E3 true. That does not look like a push toward false.
3. A margin check on distance-one sources has to run after the build, because only the build says which sources are at distance one. The commit and the SURVEY both say the check sits outside the frozen protocol and changes no status.
4. The SURVEY sentence "told nothing of which element was in question" is literally true. Every source got the same prompt, and it names three elements for all of them, so no reader was told which one separated its own source. The SURVEY never says the margin prompt matched the first readers' prompt. The prompt is committed, and afc49486 names it.
5. The SURVEY does not make "1 of 4" look safe. Lines 119-123 say the clause "survives on one element" and that a later pass "could retire the clause, and with it the sentence".

What is left is minor: the margin prompt adds a restatement and a "central comparison" scope that the first readers' prompt does not have, and the SURVEY does not say so. The scope is close to the protocol's own RETIRES rule, which requires E1 to E5 "for the same object". This is a disclosure gap, not a false sworn statement and not a wrong status.

verdicts.reason:
I could not reproduce the defect, on three counts.

1. **The frozen element definitions do not allow pooling.** Each element is tied to one comparison. E3 asks for a floor used to grade "the comparison". E4 asks for an interval "for the compared quantity". E5 says "The compared quantity is computed from the model's token log-probabilities". Pooled B10 would take E4 from the text-MMD test and E5 from the log-prob check. Those are two different compared quantities, so pooling breaks the literal wording rather than following it. The RETIRES rule and the reader prompt both say "for the same object". Reader-1 coded one object, which is what the definitions require, and disclosed the choice in the record's notes.

2. **The claimed contrast with B22 fails.** B22 is one method, logprob tracking: a permutation test on first-token top-k log-probs for one fixed prompt. Its in-vitro TinyChange runs carry E1, E2, E3 and E5 on their own:
   - E1: pruned and noised variants of the same weights, which fit E1(ii).
   - E2: the same prompt on both sides.
   - E3: original/original null tests.
   - E5: log-probs.

   The E1 quote ("the same API at different times") comes from the method definition that covers both setups. All four blind margin readers of B22 coded E1, E2, E3 and E5 true on that one method. So the two readers did not use opposite pooling conventions.

3. **Pooling leads somewhere absurd.** Pooled B10 would take E3 from the benchmark experiment, which grades quantized against full-precision on the spread of 10 repeated runs ("within one standard deviation"). On that reading B10 could carry all five elements and become a RETIRES candidate. It would do so on a paper that concludes every software check is unreliable. That is a strong sign pooling is not the protocol's reading.

What does hold up: reader-1 implicitly counted the symbolic, unvalued alpha of the MMD test as E4, while B22's reader did not. That is ordinary inter-reader variance on an element the SURVEY already calls hardest. It does not change B10's recorded distance for its coded object, the nearness list, or the sworn sentence. The margin check was defined only for distance-one sources, and B10 at distance 2 is treated like A04, B09, B11 and B15. At most this is a minor note, not a major defect.

verdicts.reason:
The finding rests on two claims, and neither survives a check.

1. **Pooling does not follow from the protocol's literal wording.** "The same object" is a class, but the element definitions attach E3 to E5 to one comparison. E3 is a floor in "the setup used for the comparison", E4 is an interval "for the compared quantity", and E5 requires "the compared quantity is computed from the model's token log-probabilities". In B10 the only E4-like test is on a Hamming-kernel MMD over sampled text: Llama-70B at full precision against INT8, 25 Wikipedia prompts. The only E5 is a different experiment: the log-prob verification across frameworks and GPUs on UltraChat queries. Taking E4 from one and E5 from the other means no single compared quantity is both log-prob based and graded by a test. The definitions exclude that. Reader-1 coded one object per comparison, and did the same for B01: the Appendix C.5 log-prob tests were set aside as a separate object, so B01 was not pushed to distance 0. The convention is consistent.

2. **B22 was not pooled the opposite way.** Its in-vitro TinyChange comparison alone carries E1, E2, E3 and E5. TinyChange includes weight pruning and parameter noising of the same trained weights, which E1(ii) names explicitly. It uses one fixed prompt, a null from 1,000 original/original tests on identical weights, and first-token logprobs. It is one method with one compared quantity. All four blind margin readers describe it that way, and three of them also land on distance 1 missing E4.

The finding's own projection also fails. To get "distance 1 missing E3" it counts B10's MMD alpha as E4 true. That alpha is never given a value: grep finds only symbolic α at lines 387, 402 and 404, and the Figure 1 caption and axes (lines 325-360) give no level. E4 demands "a stated level". B22's first reader and three of its four margin readers treat an unvalued alpha as E4 false. On that convention a pooled B10 does not miss only E3, so the claimed replacement of Xu et al. does not follow.

What remains is small. Reader-1's reason sentence says "also distance 2" for the MMD object, which implies the symbolic alpha counted as E4. That sits in the reason text for an object that was not coded, and changes no coded element, distance, status or sentence. There was also no obligation to margin-check B10: the SURVEY promised the check only for sources at distance one, and B10 is recorded at distance 2. At most this is a minor note that the one-comparison convention was not written into the frozen protocol. It is not a defect in the record or in the sworn document.

verdicts.reason: I could not reproduce this as a defect. The record's E1 coding for B09 follows the most natural reading of the frozen protocol, uses it the same way as for the other sources, and is backed by what the source actually does. Clause (i), "the same model at another time", has to allow changed weights. If it did not, it would add nothing to clause (ii), which already covers "the same trained weights". The protocol also builds its search around models that change: Q03 is "detecting changes in a deployed language model API over time" and Q08 is "behavioral drift monitoring". The RETIRES object is "a served model's behaviour against its own earlier ... self". The exclusion "was it stolen or fine-tuned from mine" sits inside a list of provenance questions between different models ("which model is this, which family"). It does not cover a developer checking their own model after an update. The record applies this line consistently. A01 and A02 are piracy or surrogate checks on fine-tuned copies, and both are coded E1 false. B22 is "the same API at different times" and B11 is an endpoint "over time", where the weights may change, and both are coded E1 true. B09 does the test itself, so this is not just framing. Line 420 says "We instruction-tune Llama3 on 5 different task clusters" to simulate an auditor checking an aligned model after an update. Line 427 says "We test Llama3 against each instruction-tuned model". So the quoted comparison is Llama3 against its own later fine-tuned selves. The protocol asks only for a verbatim quote per true element, not a quote that proves the element on its own, and the quote was found. The finding's suggested replacement is line 176, the paper's motivating question. That quote discusses the setting rather than showing the test, which fits the "does it, not discusses it" rule worse. The reader's note already discloses the stricter reading. The finding admits that no sentence, status or nearest-neighbour name changes: B09 is at distance 2, and nearest names are drawn only from distance-1 sources (B01, B14, B22). What is left is a disagreement over reading the protocol, not an error under the frozen rules.
